policies.title: Prompt user to change password before expiration

actions.message: Windows password history = ${PasswordHistoryCount}. Direct Linux equivalent is limited; closest control is pam_pwquality difok and password history modules not enabled by default.

actions.content: # Consider pam_pwhistory or stronger difok settings for password history semantics

actions.message: Windows reversible encryption is disabled. Linux target should keep one-way hashing only.

actions.comment: Keep non-reversible hash method in login.defs

actions.message: Observed Astra common-password currently uses pam_unix with gost12_512; this is stronger or comparable to SHA512 in terms of non-reversible storage.

actions.comment: Remove nullok from common-auth if present

actions.message: Current Astra already has PREVENT_NO_AUTH=${PreventNoAuth}; nullok was observed in pam_unix line and should be reviewed.

actions.message: Observed Astra config has pam_faillock deny=8 but no explicit unlock_time in common-auth; duration should be added explicitly for closer parity.

actions.comment: Template for reset counter interval via pam_faillock fail_interval

actions.message: Windows administrator lockout = ${AllowAdministratorLockout}. On Linux this is controlled by pam_faillock even_deny_root/root_unlock_time and should be enabled only after careful review.

policies.title: Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP clients

actions.message: Windows requires enhanced NTLM session security on clients. Closest Linux/Astra analogue is SMB client hardening in smb.conf or Kerberos-only access; manual review required.

policies.title: Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP servers

actions.message: Windows requires enhanced NTLM session security on servers. Closest Astra analogue is Samba server signing and stronger auth settings; manual review required.

policies.title: Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash

actions.message: Requirement is satisfied conceptually in Astra/Linux because LM hashes are not used; modern password hashing is configured separately.

policies.title: Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire

actions.message: No direct standalone analogue in Astra/Linux without additional PAM time/access policy configuration.

policies.title: Network security: LAN Manager authentication level

commands: # review and adjust if Samba is used

policies.title: Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation

actions.message: Astra/Linux typically does not expose an equivalent anonymous SID/Name translation mechanism; requirement is treated as satisfied by design.

policies.title: Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts

actions.message: Closest analogue depends on Samba configuration and local account mapping. Manual verification is required.

policies.title: Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts

actions.message: Astra/Linux does not expose SAM enumeration; anonymous account enumeration should be restricted by NSS/PAM/service configuration. Treated as conceptually satisfied.

policies.title: Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire

actions.message: No direct standalone equivalent in Astra/Linux without Samba + PAM time policy integration.

policies.title: UAC: Virtualize file and registry write failures

actions.message: Windows UAC virtualization has no direct equivalent in Astra/Linux; treat as architecture-specific limitation.

policies.title: UAC: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode

actions.message: Closest Astra/Linux analogue is polkit/sudo mediation for privileged actions; no direct 1:1 automatic mapping.

policies.title: UAC: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation

actions.message: Closest analogue is polkit/package manager authorization; manual review required.

policies.title: UAC: Switch to secure desktop when prompting for elevation

actions.message: Desktop secure-elevation model differs between Windows and Astra; manual analysis required.

policies.title: UAC: Elevation prompt behavior for administrators

actions.message: Prompt behavior maps only semantically to polkit authentication_agent behavior; not automated.

policies.title: UAC: Elevation prompt behavior for standard users

actions.message: Standard-user elevation prompts map only semantically to polkit/sudo policy; not automated.

policies.title: UAC: Only elevate signed and validated executables

actions.message: Closest analogue would require application whitelisting or package-signature enforcement; not automated in this prototype.

policies.title: Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers

actions.message: Closest analogue is restricting CUPS/polkit admin actions; manual hardening required.
No meaningful direct analogue for the tested Astra workstation profile.

policies.title: Devices: Allowed to access floppy drives

actions.message: Removable media access in Astra/Linux depends on udisks/polkit/device ACLs; not automated.

policies.title: Devices: Allowed to access CD-ROM drives

actions.message: CD/DVD access in Astra/Linux depends on group membership and polkit/udisks rules; not automated.

policies.title: Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media

actions.message: Formatting/eject rights can be controlled via polkit/udisks rules; template can be added later if needed.

policies.title: User rights: Back up files and directories

actions.message: Closest analogue is backup tooling + CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH/root privileges. Manual role mapping is required.

policies.title: User rights: Restore files and directories

actions.message: Closest analogue is restore tooling + CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE/root privileges. Manual role mapping is required.

policies.title: User rights: Load and unload device drivers

actions.message: Loading kernel modules in Astra/Linux is governed by root privileges and module signing policy; no direct safe automatic mapping.
Closest analogue is ptrace capability control (e.g., kernel.yama.ptrace_scope, CAP_SYS_PTRACE); manual review required.

policies.title: User rights: Modify firmware environment values

actions.message: Closest analogue is EFI variable management by root with efivarfs; not automatically mapped.
Unix path traversal semantics differ from Windows traverse checking; this is treated as architecture-specific.

policies.title: User rights: Manage auditing and security log

actions.message: Closest analogue is control over auditd/parsec_aud configuration by root or dedicated audit administrators.
Creating symlinks is governed by filesystem permissions in Linux; no equivalent per-user security right mapping.
Windows global object namespaces do not have a direct Linux security-right analogue.
Swap/pagefile management in Linux is root-administered and not mapped as a discrete user right.
Closest analogue is nice/rtprio limits and capabilities. Manual role/limits.conf mapping is required.

policies.title: User rights: Increase a process working set

actions.message: Closest analogue is resource limits (ulimit/systemd) rather than a direct security-right mapping.
